library.title: Components
library.proHint: Runs in every plan; saving it to the cloud needs the Maker plan
library.askAi: No good match. Ask AI which part can: “{query}”

canvas.label: Circuit canvas
canvas.help: Drag parts · drag the background to select · click a pin to start a wire · wheel to zoom, Space+drag or middle button to pan · R rotate, F flip, Ctrl+D duplicate, Ctrl+A all, M minimap, Delete, Ctrl+Z
canvas.drawing: Click to bend the wire, click a pin or hole to finish · Esc cancels
canvas.runHelp: Running: press buttons and switches on the parts, click a knob or sensor to adjust it · Stop to edit the circuit
canvas.viewHelp: View only: editing needs a larger screen
canvas.minimap: Circuit overview: click or drag to move the view
canvas.expand: Expand to full page (Esc to exit)

parts.title: {count, plural, =0 {No parts yet} one {# part} other {# parts}}

props.none: Select a part or a wire on the canvas to edit it.
props.multiple: {count, plural, one {# part selected} other {# parts selected}}
props.boardNote: The board can be moved and turned, but not deleted.

armed.red: Click a pin or hole for the red (+) probe · Esc cancels
armed.black: Click a pin or hole for the black (COM) probe · Esc cancels
armed.wire: Click a wire, or a part pin, to measure the current through it · Esc cancels
armed.part: Click a part to measure its power · Esc cancels

hint.placeRed: Place the red probe to start measuring.
hint.pickCurrent: Pick a wire or a part pin to measure current.
hint.pickPart: Pick a part to measure its power.
hint.noRun: Run the project to read live values. Resistance works without a run.
hint.stopRun: Stop the run to measure resistance
hint.open: Over range: no connection between the probes (OL).
hint.unresolved: This point is not simulated (an unused rail or an unconnected pin).
hint.floating: Nothing electrical is connected to this point.
hint.loop: Parallel path: this wire's current is not defined. Probe a part pin instead.
hint.hole: Current flows through a part pin or a wire, not a breadboard hole.
hint.ground: Current into GND is the sum of the whole circuit: probe a wire or part pin instead.
hint.powerSign: Negative power: the part delivers energy (a source).

scope.title: Oscilloscope
scope.gone: This part is no longer in the circuit: the channel reads nothing.

add.armed: Click a pin or hole to add a voltage channel · Esc cancels
add.full: All 4 channels are in use. Remove one to add another.

scope.held: Held: drag, scroll or use the arrow keys to look back. Live returns to the latest sweep.
scope.empty: Add a channel: pick a pin below or place it on the canvas.
scope.noRun: Run the project to see the traces.

note.aliasing: Sampled at 1 kHz: use the logic analyzer for faster digital signals, or a timebase below 1 ms/div for fine mode on circuits with a capacitor or inductor.
note.pwm: PWM edges are rebuilt from the timer's frequency and duty.
note.fineOn: Fine mode: between the 1 kHz readings the trace follows the solver's sub-steps.
note.fineNone: Fine mode: this circuit has no capacitor or inductor, so there is nothing finer than the 1 kHz readings. Use the logic analyzer for faster digital signals.
note.fineSlow: Fine mode was turned off: the simulation ran slower than 0.8× the chosen speed.

cursor.hint: Click to place cursor A, Shift+click for B. Arrow keys move A (with Shift: B); + and − change the timebase.

power.title: Power budget

basis.static: Estimate from each part's typical current × duty. Run the project with this tab open to measure it.
basis.measured: Measured over this run: average and peak of every 1 ms step.

power.noSupply: MCU pin / not on a supply

life.assumptions: Until {cutoff} at {current}; range: high-current bursts to light load. No Peukert effect: real alkalines give less at high current.

chart.title: Power per part over the run (stacked; the area is the energy)
chart.summary: Stacked power of {count} series, up to {max}. Use the left and right arrow keys to read each moment; the table lists every part.

power.includesOutputs: (includes what it passes to its outputs)

tidy.button: Tidy wires: recolour and straighten (preview first)
tidy.title: Tidy wires
tidy.failed: Tidy would have changed the connections, so nothing was changed. Please report this.

hints.title: Wiring hints
hints.intro: Readability tips, not safety findings. Nothing here stops a run.
hints.marker: Wiring hint: see Safety › Wiring hints
hints.none: No wiring hints: the wires are easy to follow.
hints.signalAvoid: Hint when a signal wire uses these colours

color.why: {supply} is usually +V, {ground} GND. Matching colours make a circuit easy to read and to copy onto a real breadboard.

long.title: Wire {wire} is long ({length} mm)
long.why: A shorter, straighter route is easier to follow. Tidy can straighten it.

overPart.title: Wire {wire} runs over {parts}
overPart.why: A wire drawn across a part hides its pins and labels. Tidy routes around parts where it can.

overlap.title: Wires {wire} and {other} overlap
overlap.why: Overlapping wires of different nets look connected when they are not.

rail.ground: {count} GND wires go into breadboard rows
rail.why: Wire the board once to the breadboard's {rail} rail and plug the parts into the rail: fewer, shorter wires. This is a suggestion only; Tidy never moves wire ends.
